**Bounded nilpotency.** Claim: a group `H` generated by `X` is nilpotent of class
at most `c` iff every left-normed commutator `[x_1, ..., x_(c+1)]` with all
`x_i in X` is trivial. Only the "if" direction needs proof, by induction on `c`.
- **Base case `c = 1`.** Commuting generators give an abelian group.
- **Inductive step.** Suppose all weight-`(c+1)` generator commutators vanish.
  Then each weight-`c` generator commutator `u = [x_1, ..., x_c]` satisfies
  `[u, x] = 1` for every `x in X`, so `u` is central. The subgroup `C` they
  generate is central, hence normal.
- **Quotient.** In `H/C` every weight-`c` generator commutator is trivial, so by
  induction `H/C` is nilpotent of class at most `c-1`. A central extension of a
  group of class at most `c-1` has class at most `c`.

Hence `P = <X | R>` is nilpotent of class at most `c` iff finitely many words are
trivial.
Each has a finite derivation, and the search is uniform in `(P, c)`. The union
over `c` gives `NILPOTENT_fp`, and `c = 1` gives `ABELIAN_fp`.

**Polycyclicity** (import). G. Baumslag, F. B. Cannonito, C. F. Miller III, *Some
recognizable properties of solvable groups*, Math. Z. 178 (1981) 289--295, read
from the PDF on 2026-09-12. The proof of their Theorem 3.3 runs two searches; the
second works for an arbitrary finite presentation. Verbatim: "In the second one
Tietze transforms Π repeatedly. [...] If gp(Π) is polycyclic, an honest
polycyclic presentation (cf. [3]) for gp(Π) will appear in the second search. By
Theorem 4.3 of [3] we may effectively recognize when this occurs." Here [3] is
their *Infinitely generated subgroups of finitely presented groups I*, Math. Z.
153 (1977), whose Theorem 4.3 was not read. So `POLYCYCLIC_fp` is c.e.

**Finiteness.** Todd--Coxeter enumeration of the cosets of the trivial subgroup
halts exactly when the group is finite. **Triviality** is the case where every
generator has a derivation to `1`.

**Hardness.** Each property holds for the trivial group. It is inherited by
subgroups and fails for `F_2`, so it fails for every group containing `F_2`. The
Adian--Rabin family `w -> L_w` in the route of
`amenability-of-finite-presentations-arithmetical-position` has `L_w` trivial
when `w = 1` and `F_2 <= L_w` when `w != 1`. So
`{w : w = 1}` many-one reduces to each set in `(PT1)`, and that set is
`Sigma^0_1`-complete. `∎`
